name: Advocate MCP Structured Data
author: cameronjmcewan

sections.description:
Search engines and AI assistants read structured data to understand what a
business is, where it is, and what it offers. This plugin puts your Advocate
business profile into your site’s <head> as JSON-LD, server-side, so crawlers
that do not run JavaScript can read it.

You maintain one profile on Advocate. This site follows it — there is nothing to
re-enter here when your hours, address, or services change.

Background profile updates. The profile is fetched in the background,
never while a visitor is waiting for a page. If Advocate is unreachable and a
profile was downloaded successfully before, the plugin uses it for up to 24
hours from its last validated download. It then pauses structured data until a
valid download succeeds. Unknown-age caches from older versions also pause
until refreshed. Your site keeps working.

External services

This plugin connects to Advocate (https://app.advocatemcp.com), a service run by
Advocate MCP LLC. An Advocate account and a published business profile are
required to publish structured data. Advocate offers paid service plans; review
current plans at https://app.advocatemcp.com/pricing before subscribing. Installing
or connecting this plugin does not subscribe you or charge you.

Account connection. Only after an administrator clicks Connect Advocate,
the browser opens Advocate with this website’s public address, its WordPress
admin return address, and a random temporary state value. You sign in or create
an account, choose your business, and confirm. WordPress receives only the public
business identifier and website, never your Advocate password or account token.
A new business stays private until you complete onboarding and choose to publish.
HTTPS is required, and the public website and WordPress admin must have the same
origin (their paths may differ). Manual setup remains available.

The following profile and page-view requests require a configured Business ID.
Directory packages make no plugin-initiated Advocate request before connection
or configuration. Self-hosted ZIP packages additionally check the public update
manifest described below, independently of configuration.

1. Fetching your profile. On a background refresh, about hourly, the plugin
requests https://app.advocatemcp.com/api/biz/<your-business-id>/jsonld. Only
your Business ID is sent. The reply is the JSON-LD this plugin prints. It is
data, not code — nothing is downloaded and run. This never happens while a
visitor is waiting for a page.

2. Reporting page views. After a page has finished sending, the plugin posts
to https://app.advocatemcp.com/api/edge/plugin-beacon to report that one page
view happened. It sends your Business ID, your site’s hostname, the path of the
page viewed with the query string removed, the visitor’s browser or crawler
user-agent string, the installed plugin version, and a SHA-256 hash of the
visitor’s IP address. A hash is not a guarantee of anonymity. The raw IP
address is never sent. The request does not block, so it cannot delay or break a
page. This is what lets your Advocate dashboard show visits and AI-crawler reads
on your own site.

Directory packages do not load a remote page script.

The plugin also adds a few tags to your pages’ <head> (and a Link response
header) naming Advocate’s MCP endpoint for your business, and sends requests
for your site’s /.well-known/mcp.json to Advocate’s description of it, only
when your site would otherwise answer that address with a “not found” page.
These are data; nothing is sent anywhere.

To stop profile fetching and page-view reporting, clear the
Business ID or deactivate the plugin. Turning publishing off also stops
scheduled page-view reporting. Page/CDN cache hits do not run PHP and are not
measured by this plugin.

Self-hosted distribution updates. Direct ZIP packages contain an updater
that periodically requests https://app.advocatemcp.com/wordpress-plugin/advocatemcp-structured-data.json
with the plugin version in its user-agent, even before a Business ID is set.
A copy installed before 2.5.0 lives in the advocate-agent folder and requests
https://app.advocatemcp.com/wordpress-plugin/advocate-agent.json instead; both
addresses offer this same release.
The manifest can offer a plugin ZIP from the same service. Directory packages
omit this updater and use WordPress.org’s standard plugin update mechanism.

Advocate’s terms of service: https://app.advocatemcp.com/terms
Advocate’s privacy policy: https://app.advocatemcp.com/privacy
sections.installation:
1. Install and activate Advocate MCP Structured Data. If using a directory release,
    use Plugins → Add New. If using a downloaded ZIP, use Upload Plugin.
  2. Open Settings → Advocate and choose Connect Advocate. Sign in or create
    your Advocate account, choose the business, and confirm the website.
  3. Complete onboarding in Advocate if your business is new. Publication and any
    subscription are separate choices; connecting the plugin does not publish.
  4. For a published profile, open WordPress setup in Advocate and select
    Check connection to observe whether the latest profile is on your site.

A download prepared in your Advocate account can still configure a matching
website automatically. Existing settings are kept, including disabled publishing.
To use manual setup, enter the Business ID (the final part of the Advocate profile
URL) in Settings → Advocate. Automatic connection preserves an existing disabled
publishing setting; enable it explicitly when you are ready.

A connection attempt expires after two hours. If it expires, your WordPress
account/site changes, or somebody edits these plugin settings while you are away,
start Connect Advocate again. Existing settings are kept on a refused callback.
The first profile update runs in the background; Refresh now retries it.
sections.faq:
Where can I get help?

Use the contact form at https://app.advocatemcp.com/contact or email
support@advocatemcp.com.

I already use Yoast or Rank Math. Should I use both?

Probably not both for the same business. Two descriptions of one business on one
page can confuse crawlers. The settings page warns you when it detects another
SEO plugin — ask Advocate which one to keep.

How quickly does a profile edit reach my site?

The plugin checks for updates about once an hour. Choose Refresh now to check
sooner. Cached pages may need to be cleared before they show the update.

Automatic checks run through WordPress scheduled tasks (WP-Cron), which only
run when your site is visited or when your host triggers them, so there is no
fixed delivery deadline. “Refresh now” checks immediately; a successful check
updates this plugin’s own copy of the profile, not caches in front of your site.

What happens if Advocate is down?

The saved profile can appear on newly generated pages for up to 24 hours after
its last validated download. Failed retries do not extend that time. After
that, publishing pauses until a valid download succeeds. The settings page
shows the pause and offers Refresh now. This uses the WordPress server clock;
keep it synchronized. It does not guarantee a deadline across clock changes.

Page/CDN caches may still contain older HTML and must be cleared separately.
This is an outage-age limit, not an authenticated remote withdrawal signal.
Updating the downloadable ZIP does not update existing installed copies;
replace the installed plugin through your normal WordPress update procedure.

Does this support WordPress multisite?

Activate and configure Advocate separately on each site. New network activation
is refused, and one business is never configured for all sites. Public website
path and nondefault port must match as well as hostname. Deactivation clears
that site’s refresh tasks and cached profile while preserving its settings;
reactivation needs a fresh download. Uninstall removes plugin settings too.
When two copies of the plugin are installed (see the 2.5.0 changelog), the
notice appears on each site’s own Plugins screen, not on the network Plugins
screen. A network-wide delete of the earlier copy restores settings only when
this copy is loaded in that Network Admin request, that is, active on the main
site; if it is active only on sub-sites, nothing is saved anywhere.

Legacy network deactivation cleans the current network, while uninstall checks
all networks because plugin files are shared. Automatic cleanup is limited to
100 sites. A larger scope is refused before any site is changed. A database or
cache failure stops cleanup with an error; resolve it and retry. Completed
sites may already be cleaned. Neither operation purges existing page/CDN HTML.

How does an administrator remove Advocate from more than 100 sites?

Use a maintenance window and a verified backup. Stop incoming PHP/cron work and
drain existing workers first; older plugin code does not honor the new inactive
marker. Inventory every site across every network. Use WP-CLI with
–skip-plugins=advocatemcp-structured-data to deactivate the plugin on every network and
any separately active site without loading its bounded automatic hooks. Keep
the plugin files in place until every site’s cleanup is verified.

For each site URL in that inventory, run the following with the current source
installed (a copy installed before 2.5.0 uses the advocate-agent folder and
main file name in both places). Replace the example URL. This reuses the plugin’s per-site cleanup,
then removes settings only after that cleanup succeeds. Stop on any error:

wp --url='https://example.com/site/' --skip-plugins=advocatemcp-structured-data eval '
require WP_PLUGIN_DIR . "/advocatemcp-structured-data/advocatemcp-structured-data.php";
advocate_deactivate_site();
$missing = new stdClass();
foreach ( [ "advocate_agent_settings", "advocate_setup_import", "advocate_setup_notice", "advocate_connect_attempt", "advocate_lifecycle" ] as $key ) {
    delete_option( $key );
    if ( get_option( $key, $missing ) !== $missing ) {
        WP_CLI::error( "Cleanup failed for " . $key . "; resolve storage errors and retry." );
    }
}
WP_CLI::success( "Advocate data and refresh tasks cleared for this site." );'

Retain a successful receipt for every site and verify that no Advocate refresh
task or plugin data remains. Only then remove the shared plugin directory and
clear page/CDN caches. A site-level Delete button does not bypass the global
100-site uninstall preflight. This operator procedure still requires a staging
rehearsal for your WordPress/WP-CLI and cache configuration.
sections.changelog:
2.5.0

  • Renamed to Advocate MCP Structured Data (slug advocatemcp-structured-data)
    for the WordPress.org plugin directory. A copy that updates in place keeps
    its settings, cached profile and scheduled refreshes unchanged. Switching
    from the earlier advocate-agent folder to this one by deactivating the old
    copy clears its cached profile and refresh schedule, as any deactivation
    does; this copy downloads the profile again within a minute of activation.
  • Values read from the request (the visitor’s user agent, address and path,
    and the account connection callback’s method and query) pass through
    WordPress sanitizers before use. Translations load through WordPress itself.
  • A site holding both the earlier advocate-agent folder and this one can
    activate only one; the active copy says so on the Plugins screen. Switch in
    this order: deactivate the earlier copy, activate this one, and only then
    delete the earlier copy — while this copy is active it puts back anything
    the earlier copy’s uninstall removes. Deleting the earlier copy before this
    one is active removes the settings. Deleting this copy while the earlier one
    is installed leaves the settings for it.

2.4.0

  • Publishes a per-business pointer to Advocate’s MCP server alongside the
    structured data: <link>/<meta> discovery tags, a schema.org WebAPI block,
    and a Link response header. The render path still performs no I/O.
  • Directory packages do not load a remote page script.
  • /.well-known/mcp.json on this site redirects to Advocate’s manifest for
    this business, only when nothing else on the site answers that address.

2.3.0

  • Connect an Advocate account without copying a Business ID; preserve disabled
    publishing and refuse stale, expired, wrong-user or wrong-site callbacks.
  • Consume each connection and apply settings together; replay cannot overwrite
    later local settings. Keep new business profiles private through onboarding.
  • Prepare an explicit directory package without the self-hosted update channel
    or business-specific setup data; preserve direct-distribution compatibility.
  • Describe account connection, plugin-version reporting, service plans and update
    requests accurately. Compatibility metadata reflects tested versions only.

2.2.2

  • Self-hosted update channel: the plugin now carries an Update URI header and
    checks Advocate’s version manifest for new releases, so WordPress offers
    updates without a WordPress.org listing. Update packages are requested only
    from app.advocatemcp.com over HTTPS.
  • The traffic beacon reports the installed plugin version so Advocate can show
    which version each site runs.

2.2.1

  • Pause newly generated structured data after 24 hours without a validated
    profile download, including unknown-age legacy caches; show the pause in
    settings. Failed refreshes cannot renew the deadline.
  • Validate the public site path and port on downloaded and cached profiles,
    including every supplied identity anchor.
  • Refuse new network activation, bound legacy multisite cleanup, clear every
    refresh event and fence late refresh workers across deactivation/reactivation.
  • Preserve cleanup retry state and report storage failures before uninstall can
    remove the inactive marker. Page/CDN cache removal remains an operator step.

2.2.0

  • Downloads prepared in Advocate can configure the business automatically on
    the matching website. Existing business settings and disabled publishing are
    preserved. Generic downloads still support manual setup.

2.1.0

  • After a page has been sent, the plugin now tells Advocate one page view
    happened (which page, which browser or crawler), so your Advocate dashboard
    can show visits and AI-crawler reads on your own site. The visitor’s IP
    address never leaves your server — only a one-way hash is sent. Nothing
    about this waits on Advocate or can slow a visitor down.

2.0.0

  • The profile is now fetched in the background. Earlier versions could make a
    visitor wait up to five seconds when the cache was cold.
  • Failed fetches are remembered briefly instead of retried on every page view.
  • The block is no longer added to 404, search, or feed pages.
  • Warns when another SEO plugin is already publishing business schema.
  • Refuses to publish a profile that is anchored to a domain other than this one.
  • The settings page reports what was last published and when.
  • Setup is one field. The Agent Query URL and Business Name fields are gone.
  • Removed /.well-known/mcp.json. It advertised endpoints that no longer exist.

1.1.0

  • Structured data injection.

1.0.0

  • Initial release.
